stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dP}{dt} = - 3 P + 9 t + 15 \). Without drawing it, describe the field of slope segments for this equation: where the segments are horizontal, where they have positive slope, and where they have negative slope.

answer_key.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( P = 3 t + 5 \), have positive slope where \( P < 3 t + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( P > 3 t + 5 \).

worked_solution.text: A segment is horizontal where the right side is 0: \( - 3 P + 9 t + 15 = 0 \) exactly when \( P = 3 t + 5 \), which is the line \( P = 3 t + 5 \).
The right side equals \( -3\left(P - 3 t - 5\right) \), so its sign is positive where \( P < 3 t + 5 \) and negative where \( P > 3 t + 5 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the slope on each side of the locus

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( P = 5 \), have positive slope where \( P < 5 \), and have negative slope where \( P > 5 \).
options.derivation: the slope read as depending on P alone, the t term ignored, so the segments would match along horizontal lines

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( t = 3 P + 5 \), have positive slope where \( t < 3 P + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( t > 3 P + 5 \).
options.derivation: each lattice point read with its coordinates exchanged, so t and P trade places

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( P = 3 t + 5 \), have positive slope where \( P > 3 t + 5 \), and have negative slope where \( P < 3 t + 5 \).
options.derivation: the horizontal row located but the tilt on each side taken from the look of a familiar field instead of from a computed slope
